bull.b: TTM revenue growth and a move to roughly 30% gross margin show improving commercial traction and unit economics. If retained, this combination can provide a stronger base for scaling the connected-equipment model, although profitability still depends on reducing operating costs.

Positive equity of about $3.3M in TTM, versus negative equity in 2021–2023, indicates the capital base has improved from prior distress. This gives the company a better solvency foundation over the next several months, even though leverage and losses remain material.

Exchanging $7.69M of unsecured convertible notes for preferred stock and terminating the prior debt facility reshapes near-term obligations. Reduced debt-facility exposure may ease refinancing pressure and improve financial flexibility, although the senior preferred claims remain a burden.

bear.b: TTM operating losses remain larger than revenue and net margin is roughly -159%, showing that higher sales have not yet translated into a viable earnings model. Persistent deep losses can consume capital, limit self-funded investment, and keep the company reliant on financing.

Materially negative TTM operating and free cash flow shows the business is consuming cash rather than funding operations internally. Continued burn can accelerate reliance on external capital, constrain investment in growth, and increase vulnerability if financing becomes less available.

The new preferred structure ranks ahead of common equity in liquidation and includes conversion mechanics, creating a continuing capital-structure overhang. Potential conversion can dilute common shareholders, while senior claims may limit flexibility in future financing and distributions.
